title: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference
summary: Given an integer array of 2n elements, divide it into two arrays of n elements each to minimize the absolute difference between their sums.
statement: Given an integer array of 2n elements, divide it into two arrays of n elements each to minimize the absolute difference between their sums. Return the smallest possible absolute difference.
constraints: nums has 2n elements with n at most 15; values may be negative.
Split all elements into two groups of exactly n elements.
Return the minimum absolute difference between group sums.
hints: Enumerating all 2^(2n) subsets is too large, but each half has at most fifteen elements.
Group subset sums of each half by chosen count; pair complementary counts and binary-search near half the total.
For each left sum using c items, search sorted right sums using n-c items near total/2-left.
Every legal n-item group splits into one complementary-count pair, and the closest combined sum to half the total minimizes |total-2*chosen|.
editorial: Every legal n-item group splits into one complementary-count pair, and the closest combined sum to half the total minimizes |total-2*chosen|.

tests.explanation: Splitting [3,9] and [7,3] gives sums twelve and ten, difference two.
Each group receives one value, producing absolute difference seventy-two.
